summary: split build-time NEXT_PUBLIC_* into /etc/guru-web.public.env so npm run build can inline them
description:
Live symptom: app boots cleanly (no journalctl errors), homepage returns 200, but the rendered HTML has empty NEXT_PUBLIC_* values:

  publishableKey:""
  signInUrl:""
  domain:""

(both Clerk and Stripe publishable keys, plus NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL). Clerk's client SDK silently fails to initialize → users can't sign in → 'app not working'.

Cause: Next.js bakes NEXT_PUBLIC_* into the client bundle at 'next build' time. systemd's EnvironmentFile=/etc/guru-web.env feeds the runtime process only — not the build step. deploy.sh runs 'npm ci && npm run build' as user 'deploy' with no env loaded, so all NEXT_PUBLIC_* compile to empty strings. Boot check passes because the runtime DOES see the vars, but the bundle was already shipped empty.

Fix: split the env file by trust boundary.

  /etc/guru-web.public.env  — NEXT_PUBLIC_* only — mode 0644 (already public — they ship in client JS)
  /etc/guru-web.env         — secrets only — mode 0600 root:guru (unchanged)

  systemd unit gets two EnvironmentFile= lines (merged at runtime).
  deploy.sh sources only the public file before 'npm run build'.

Done when:
- deploy/deploy.sh sources /etc/guru-web.public.env before 'npm run build'; fails fast if file missing/unreadable
- deploy/guru-web.service has both EnvironmentFile= lines
- deploy/README.md documents the split, perms, and which keys live in which file
- after redeploy: 'curl -s https://guru-ai.org/ | grep -oE "publishableKey\":\"[^\"]*\""' shows real pk_test_...

resolution.note: deploy.sh sources /etc/guru-web.public.env before npm run build (fails fast if unreadable). systemd unit takes both EnvironmentFile= lines. README documents perms + which keys live where + redeploy-required gotcha for publishable key rotation. Verification: 'curl -s https://guru-ai.org/ | grep -oE "publishableKey\":\"[^\"]*\""' should return a real pk_test_... after redeploy.
